title: Immunostaining Protocol for Non-Adherent Cells Using Centrifugal Filters
author: Miyazawa, Kawai, et al.

steps.title: Maintain cell lines
steps.instruction: Culture K562 in IMDM + 10 % FBS + 1 % penicillin/streptomycin; Jurkat in RPMI‑1640 + 10 % FBS + 1 % penicillin/streptomycin; HUDEP‑2 in StemSpan SFEM + 1 µg/mL doxycycline, 1 µM dexamethasone, 50 ng/mL SCF, 3 U/mL EPO, 1 % penicillin/streptomycin. Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Harvest and count cells
steps.instruction: Collect cells from each culture and determine cell concentration using a hemocytometer.

steps.title: Maintain HeLa and RPE-1
steps.instruction: Culture HeLa in DMEM‑high glucose + 10 % FBS + 1 % penicillin/streptomycin; RPE‑1 in DMEM/F‑12 + 10 % FBS + 1 % penicillin/streptomycin. Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Detach cells for passaging with trypsin‑EDTA.

steps.title: Synchronize and collect mitotic cells
steps.instruction: Add nocodazole to medium to 150 nM (HeLa) or 300 nM (RPE‑1) and incubate 12–15 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Shake dishes to release mitotic cells. Collect medium, centrifuge 200 g × 2 min, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1.25 mL D‑PBS (per 90 mm dish), centrifuge 200 g × 2 min, discard supernatant, resuspend in 1.25 mL fresh culture medium, incubate 30 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ to release from nocodazole arrest, then count cells with a hemocytometer.

steps.title: Load cells onto filter
steps.instruction: Apply 100 µL cell suspension (5 × 10⁴ cells for K562, Jurkat, HUDEP‑2; 2 × 10⁴ cells for HeLa) onto an Ultrafree‑MC column with a 0.65 µm PVDF membrane (optional 0.45 µm membrane – use 300 g centrifugation; optional Ultrafree‑CL for larger area; optional pre‑wash with 1× PBS). Add 400 µL 1× PBS, centrifuge 100 g × 1 min, discard flow‑through.

steps.title: Fix cells on filter
steps.instruction: Choose fixation: (a) add 300 µL 4 % PFA, incubate 20‑25 °C 30 min; or (b) add 300 µL cold methanol (‑20 °C), incubate at ‑20 °C 5 min. Centrifuge 100 g × 1 min, discard flow‑through.

steps.title: Wash post‑fixation
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL 1× PBS, centrifuge 100 g × 1 min, discard. Repeat two more times for a total of three PBS washes. Samples may be stored in PBS at 4 °C for ≥1 day.

steps.title: Block non‑specific binding
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL blocking solution, incubate 20‑25 °C 30 min (optimize composition/time as needed). Centrifuge 100 g × 1 min, discard flow‑through.

steps.title: Incubate with primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL primary antibody diluted in blocking solution, incubate 20‑25 °C 60 min (optimize concentration/time). Centrifuge 100 g × 1 min, discard flow‑through. Wash: add 300 µL 1× PBS, centrifuge 100 g × 1 min, discard; repeat twice for three PBS washes.

steps.title: Incubate with secondary antibodies
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL secondary antibody diluted in blocking solution, incubate 20‑25 °C 30 min in the dark (prevent fluorescence fading). Centrifuge 100 g × 1 min, discard flow‑through. Wash: add 300 µL 1× PBS, centrifuge 100 g × 1 min, discard; repeat twice for three PBS washes.

steps.title: Final wash and mount
steps.instruction: Immediately after the last PBS wash, proceed to mounting as described in the subsequent mounting section.

steps.title: Lyse cells for centrosome isolation
steps.instruction: From 1 × 10⁷ mitotic HeLa or RPE‑1 cells, treat with 2 µM cytochalasin D at 37 °C 20 min. Centrifuge 500 g × 2 min, discard supernatant. Resuspend pellet in 4 mL 1× PBS + 2 µM cytochalasin D, centrifuge 500 g × 2 min; repeat wash once. Resuspend in 1 mL washing buffer, keep on ice (or 4 °C). Centrifuge 500 g × 2 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant. Resuspend in 1 mL lysis buffer, rotate 4 °C 45 min. Centrifuge 5,000 g × 2 min at 4 °C, collect supernatant. Add DNase I to 2 U/mL, incubate 4 °C 30 min with gentle rotation.

steps.title: Separate centrosomes by sucrose gradient
steps.instruction: Layer 160 µL 60 % sucrose at bottom of an ultracentrifuge tube, gently overlay ~950 µL cell lysate (from previous step). Centrifuge 25,000 g × 30 min at 4 °C. Discard top 630 µL supernatant, gently remix remaining lysate with cushion. In a new tube, layer 400 µL each of 70 %, 50 %, and 35 % sucrose (bottom to top) to form a gradient. Load the mixed lysate onto the top, centrifuge 130,000 g × 90 min at 4 °C. Collect 150 µL fractions from the top; centrosomes are enriched in fractions 4–6. Samples may be flash‑frozen in liquid N₂ and stored at ‑80 °C for ≥2 months.

steps.title: Capture centrosomes on filter
steps.instruction: Mix 15–30 µL of a centrosome‑enriched fraction with 400 µL 1× PBS. Transfer to an Ultrafree‑MC column equipped with a 0.1 µm or 0.22 µm PVDF membrane (choose pore size based on structure size). Centrifuge 3,000 g × 1 min, discard flow‑through.

steps.title: Fix centrosomes on filter
steps.instruction: Add 350 µL cold methanol (‑20 °C), incubate on ice 3 min. Centrifuge 3,000 g × 1 min, discard flow‑through. Add 400 µL 1× PBS, centrifuge 3,000 g × 1 min, discard; repeat PBS wash once more (total two PBS washes). Samples may be kept in PBS at 4 °C for ≥1 day.

steps.title: Block filter for centrosomes
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL blocking solution, incubate 20‑25 °C 15 min (optimize composition if needed). Centrifuge 3,000 g × 1 min, discard flow‑through.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation (centrosomes)
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL primary antibody diluted in blocking solution, incubate 20‑25 °C 60 min. Centrifuge 3,000 g × 1 min, discard flow‑through. Wash: add 400 µL 1× PBS, centrifuge 3,000 g × 1 min, discard; repeat once for a total of two PBS washes.

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation (centrosomes)
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL secondary antibody solution, incubate 20‑25 °C 30 min in the dark (prevent fluorescence fading). Centrifuge 3,000 g × 1 min, discard flow‑through. Wash: add 400 µL 1× PBS, centrifuge 3,000 g × 1 min, discard; add 300 µL 1× PBS, centrifuge 3,000 g × 1 min, discard.

steps.title: Final wash and mount (centrosomes)
steps.instruction: Immediately after the last PBS wash, proceed to mounting as described in the mounting section.

description: Immunostaining of adherent cells is typically facilitated by their ability to attach to substrates such as glass. This adhesion allows for easy exchange of solutions, including fixation solutions and antibodies. However, immunostaining becomes challenging for certain cell types due to their lack of adhesive properties. To date, immunostaining of non-adherent cells has commonly been achieved through immobilizing the cells by centrifuging them onto substrates using specialized equipment like Cytospin, or artificially inducing adhesion through coatings of substrates with chemical compounds.1,2,3,4 Similar challenges arise when attempting to immunostain cellular structures in cell lysate or isolated from cells.5,6,7 Here, we present an alternative approach for immunostaining non-adherent cells using centrifugal filter devices equipped with a polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) membrane. The devices capture cells or cellular structures on the filter membranes while allowing the exchange of solutions necessary for immunostaining. This method eliminates the need for specialized machines like Cytospin or additional reagents, making it more accessible. In this protocol, we demonstrate the immunostaining of K562 and Jurkat cells, human leukemia cell lines, and HUDEP-2, a human erythroid progenitor cell line, as representative models of non-adherent cells.8,9,10 Additionally, we present the staining of suspended HeLa cells, an adherent cell line, indicating its potential application for analyzing adherent cell suspensions, for example, during cell sorting experiments or when cell adhesion is affected. As an example of cellular structures, we also show the staining of isolated centrosomes from mitotic HeLa and RPE-1 cells.
